summary: Connection resets and partial outputs during extended generation after large multi-part priming
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated connection resets (client-side ECONNRESET) followed by HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout and truncated streamed outputs when issuing generation requests with large max_tokens and a multipart system/user priming payload. Impact: LexaHealth production feature (clinical summarization) partially failing — ~15% of long-run requests are returning truncated output or 504s during peak hours, causing user-visible errors and retries. Observed behavior: initial tokens stream normally for 10-40s, then stream stalls and the client sees a TCP reset or receives a 504. Reproduces consistently for certain priming shapes (system prompt + 6 x document embeddings + a long JSON instruction block) and high max_tokens (>= 15,000). Timeline: 2026-03-08 09:12 customer first report; 09:25 Support requested logs and example payload; 10:05 customer provided sample request and trace IDs; 14:40 initial SRE triage; 2026-03-09 engineering repro and hypothesis. Goal: identify root cause and provide mitigation/workaround for customer as soon as possible.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use Redwood API endpoint in us-east with model redwood-open-13b.
2) Build a multi-part priming payload: a) system prompt (~2.5k tokens) b) 6 documents (each ~1.2k tokens) c) a JSON-formatted instruction block (~1.5k tokens).
3) Set max_tokens to 16000 and streaming on.
4) Issue request over HTTP/2 with client that keeps the stream open for streaming chunks.
5) Observe stable streaming for initial tokens, then stream stalls at ~30-60s and client sees ECONNRESET or receives a 504 response and truncated output.
logs:
Customer sample trace_id: trace-lexa-20260308-09:25:ab12cd; Gateway logs show 504 at 2026-03-08T09:26:11Z with upstream status 'stream-terminated'. Serving runtime traces show: [serving-runtime] span=stream_dispatcher finalizer_wait=32s queue_len=18 kernel_swap=0.014s msg='stream window exhaustion'
Snippet from SRE trace: 
  INFO 2026-03-09T10:12:22Z streamer: client=lexa-us-east; request_id=SUP-476582-01; bytes_sent=420120; last_chunk_offset=412000; stall_start=2026-03-09T10:12:19Z
  ERROR 2026-03-09T10:12:51Z api-gateway: upstream-reset request_id=SUP-476582-01 upstream=stream-worker-7 reason='connection reset by peer'
hypothesis: 1) Long priming shapes cause uneven tokenization and bursty compute which stresses the streaming window and finalizer queue, leading to transient window exhaustion and upstream connection resets. 2) Autoscaling for dedicated pools hasn't reacted quickly to this workload shape, producing queue growth and delayed KV/cache flushes. 3) In some cases a combination of HTTP/2 flow-control window limits and buffer GC results in reset from the worker process.
mitigation_and_workarounds: Provided immediate mitigations to customer: 1) Reduce max_tokens to <= 8,000 for request bursts to avoid the long finalizer queue. 2) Break priming into two separate requests (shorter priming + follow-up context) and stitch outputs client-side. 3) Temporarily pin requests to the 'burst' routing policy (engineers provided route token) and disable aggressive batching by setting header X-Redwood-Batch=none. 4) If on Dedicated, increase reserved headroom and adjust autoscaler min_replicas (support can enact this for enterprise customers).
next_steps: 1) Engineering to instrument streaming-window metrics at finer granularity and add alert for finalizer_wait > 10s (INT-4211). 2) Prototype a patch to reduce buffer amplification under bursty tokenization and to extend HTTP/2 flow-control window for streams > 60s. 3) Evaluate batching heuristics to prefer serialization for very large max_tokens. 4) Communicate recommended client-side best-practices to LexaHealth (support will send a guidance doc).
comments: 2026-03-08 09:33 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged — requested full request/response sample and customer headers. Asked LexaHealth for peak request times and whether Dedicated or Hosted.
2026-03-08 10:10 - LexaHealth (Customer): Provided sample payload and traces. Confirmed production on Hosted (us-east) and that failures affect ~15% of long-run jobs during 09:00-11:00 window.

2026-03-09 14:42 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Reproduced locally with similar priming shape. Observed a spike in finalizer latency and a short period of stream window stall. Opened INT-4211 to track runtime metrics additions.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Priya Shah (Engineer): Deployed a targeted config increase to stream window timeout on a small subset of workers. Preliminary customer testing shows reduced resets but tail 504s still occur under load.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Marcus Nguyen (SRE): Rolling plan to push mitigation patch to staging for further validation; final resolution pending root-cause change to runtime buffering logic. Updated customer with recommended temporary workarounds.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary stream-window and buffer config changes were rolled to a limited pool and customer confirmed improved success rate. Engineering has a follow-up internal task (INT-4211) to implement a permanent fix in the serving-runtime to handle bursty long-context tokenization. Customer to track impact and report any regressions; ticket remains In Progress until fix merged and deployed.
customer_impact_summary: Approx. 15% of long-context generation attempts during peak window returned truncated outputs or 504s, leading to visible errors in LexaHealth's clinical summarization feature. Workarounds reduced failure rate to ~3% in the restricted test channel.
follow_up_actions: 1) Notify product and DX to add guidance to 'best-practices for long priming' in docs. 2) Monitor stream-window and finalizer_wait alerts for 72 hours post-deploy. 3) Schedule postmortem if failures exceed 1% in next 7 days.
priority_rationale: P1 due to enterprise customer production impact with partial service degradation and potential downstream clinical workflow effects.
